title: I built a free civ game where reaching space opens a bigger map, using Claude Code and Grok. Notes on the split
author: albertsimondev
selftext:
Play (free, browser, no account): [https://vaigames.com/vybeciv/](https://vaigames.com/vybeciv/)



VybeCiv is a single-player civ-style 4X with nested maps. Earth plays like a normal civ game. Reaching orbit collapses Earth into one hex on a Solar System map, and later Sol becomes one tile in a galaxy. Older tiers keep producing under a governor while you play the new one.



How the work was split:

Me: the design, the tier idea, a written spec for each feature, playtesting, and deciding what stays.

Claude Code: wrote most of the code from those specs. It's PixiJS v8, a static site, and saves live in the browser.

Grok: design and balance feedback when I couldn't tell if a number was off.

Suno: the music.



What worked best was writing a short spec per feature before asking for any code, rather than chatting a feature into existence. \[one concrete example, e.g. how you specced the Earth to Solar System collapse\]



Where it struggled: \[the honest one, e.g. keeping three map tiers in sync, or the AI opponents\]. The late-game AI is still weak and onboarding is rough, so that's next.



Two questions for people doing similar things:

1. Has anyone gotten LLM-written game AI to plan more than a turn or two ahead?

2. Any luck having an agent playtest a turn-based game for balance?
